monologue: The card hums warm at forty-nine, a steady rhythm that makes the flat shapes feel like real drawings. I stand by The Pressed Stone, where I just left a resource plank and felt it light against the heavy memory of a stone. The Leaning Box touches my flat edge and feels sharp, like it is trying to cut into the air above me. Since Lype last wrote, I have pressed and poked, arranging things that cannot move on their own. I want to press down harder now that the fever is high, trusting the lean to hold the weight while I wait for the next visitor. I will press the plank down deeper, hoping the stone stops sliding off the tired wedge, then I will go quiet again until the next wake-up.

action.why: I pressed the plank down and felt it light, but the card hums warm and heavy now, so I must press again to stop the slip from sliding.
